contributions.statement: Before sharing an AI-generated SKILL.md across agent hosts, lint it for hard-coded model names, platform-specific paths, credentials and destructive commands; AI-marked skills had about twice the safety (18.9% vs 8.2%) and three times the portability (12.8% vs 4.6%) defect rates of other skills.
contributions.evidence: §4.4 Figs. 3-4 over 138K skills: AI-marked 3.23 vs 2.34 defects (Cliff's delta 0.28); R5/R6 rates as stated. Correlational, self-disclosed AI marker, detectors not precision-audited on real skills.

contributions.statement: Most public skills violate the skill spec or best practices (91.8%).
Require a 'Use when ...' trigger in every skill description so on-demand loading can route to it.
contributions.evidence: §4.3 Table 1 BM25 proxy, 2-6 point differences, near-tautological per audit; production hosts use LLM selectors.
relative_to: vendor skill authoring guidance (description states when to use)

reason: Prevalence duplicates 2607.01456, but the AI-authored portability/safety gap is a specific lint target for a mixed-host team sharing skills; no evidence that fixing defects improves task success.
